  • Core invariants (apply in every mode) — nine rules
  • 1. The user owns `raw/`. The LLM owns `wiki/`.
  • 2. Every operation logs to `wiki/log.md`.
  • 3. Every new or significantly-updated page touches `wiki/index.md`.
  • 4. Cross-reference aggressively.
  • 5. Cite back to `raw/`.
  • 6. Flag contradictions, don’t silently overwrite.
  • 7. Rewrite `wiki/hot.md` after every ingest.

google/cloud/google-cloud-waf-reliability

Catalog entry: Skills by Google Cloud
Source documentation: https://github.com/google/skills/blob/main/skills/cloud/google-cloud-waf-reliability/SKILL.md

Function: Generates reliability-focused guidance for Google Cloud workloads based on the design principles and recommendations in the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework.

When to use it: Use when the user asks about reliability-related topics like workload uptime, designing for high availability (HA) or DR, setting and meeting RTO/RPO targets, SRE best practices, backup strategies, multi-region failover, or fault-tolerant architecture on Google Cloud. Don’t use for other Well-Architected Framework pillars such as Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, or Security, or for hands-on resource deployment and live incident troubleshooting.

Usage guidance is taken from the skill’s own trigger description or usage section.

google/cloud/google-cloud-waf-sustainability

Catalog entry: Skills by Google Cloud
Source documentation: https://github.com/google/skills/blob/main/skills/cloud/google-cloud-waf-sustainability/SKILL.md

Function: Generates sustainability-focused guidance for Google Cloud workloads based on the design principles and recommendations in the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework (WAF).

When to use it: Use when the user asks to assess, design, or optimize Google Cloud workloads for sustainability—including the shared responsibility model, selecting low-carbon regions (CFE%), reducing resource and AI/ML energy waste, designing efficient software and storage lifecycles, or measuring and tracking emissions using Google Cloud Carbon Footprint. Don’t use for financial cost reduction (use google-cloud-waf-cost-optimization), latency and throughput tuning (use google-cloud-waf-performance-optimization), or high availability and disaster recovery (use google-cloud-waf-reliability).

Usage guidance is taken from the skill’s own trigger description or usage section.

Function: Animated technical diagrams from plain English or Mermaid, self-contained HTML/SVG

When to use it: Use this skill whenever the user asks for a flowchart, workflow, pipeline, process diagram, state machine, system architecture, infrastructure, cloud, microservices, or network topology diagram — and especially when they mention “animated”, “flowing”, “dynamic”, “alive”, “GIF-like”, or want a diagram for a landing page, README, docs, or product demo.
